data.name: Ezrian
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew name 'Ezra'. This name is often translated as 'help', 'strength' or 'God is my helper'. In the Bible, Ezra is a priest, a scribe, and a leader of the Jews who returned to Jerusalem from exile. He played a crucial role in the rebuilding of the temple and the teaching of the law to the people.

in_hebrew.name: עזריאן
in_hebrew.long_meaning: עזריאן הוא שם פרטי שמקורו בעברית ומשמעותו 'עזר יי ה' הוא עוזרי'. השם מורכב משתי מילים: 'עזר' שפירושו עזרה או סיוע, ו'יי' שהוא קיצור של שם ה', ו'הוא עוזרי' שפירושו שהוא עוזרי או הוא עזר לי. השם עזריאן נמצא בשימוש בקרב הק komunidades היהודיות והנוצריות כאחד.

in_greek.name: Εζριαν
in_greek.meaning: Ο Θεός είναι η βοήθειά μου
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Εζριαν προέρχεται από την εβραϊκή γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'Ο Θεός είναι η βοήθειά μου'. Το όνομα αποτελείται από δύο λέξεις: 'עזר' (εζερ) που σημαίνει βοήθεια ή υποστήριξη, και 'יי' (Yah) που είναι συντομογραφία του ονόματος του Θεού, και 'μου' που σημαίνει μου ή για μένα. Το όνομα Εζριαν χρησιμοποιείται και στις κοινότητες των Εβραίων και των Χριστιανών.

in_latin.name: Ezrian
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Ezrian originem habet in lingua hebraica et significat 'Deus est mea adiutorium'. Nomen constat ex duabus vocibus: 'עזר' (ezar) quod significat adiutorium vel auxilium, et 'יי' (Yah) quod est abbreviatio nominis Dei, et 'mei' quod significat meus vel mihi. Nomen Ezrian in usu est apud communitates tam Iudaeorum quam Christianorum.

in_english.name: Ezrian
in_english.meaning: God is my helper or God helps me
in_english.long_meaning: The name Ezrian originates from Hebrew roots and means 'God is my helper' or 'God helps me'. It is derived from two Hebrew words: 'ezar' (עזר) meaning help or assistance, and 'Yah' (יי) which is a shortened form of God's name. The name Ezrian holds significant spiritual meaning, implying a strong reliance on God's support and guidance. Historically, the name has been used in both Jewish and Christian communities, symbolizing faith and trust in divine providence.

historical_references.reference: Ezra led the second Jewish exile from Babylon to Jerusalem in 458 BC, bringing the Law of Moses and other sacred texts back to the Jewish community. He was a scribe, priest, and a leader of the returning exiles. The name 'Ezra' is believed to mean 'help' or 'aid' in Hebrew.

Saint Ezra, also known as Ezra of Bethlehem, was a 5th-century Syrian monk and archimandrite who lived a life of great asceticism and sanctity. His feast day is celebrated on February 16 in the Eastern Orthodox Church. The origin of the name 'Ezra' in this context is not entirely clear, but it may have been given in honor of the biblical figure Ezra.
